note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Patient presents with a 3-week history of worsening lower back pain radiating to the right leg, associated with numbness and weakness.
- Physical examination revealed decreased right ankle reflex and positive straight leg raise test; MRI pending; management includes analgesia and neurology referral.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Lower back pain with radiculopathy
- Onset: 3 weeks; progression: worsening intensity; symptoms: radiating pain to right leg, numbness, weakness.
- Systems review: No bowel or bladder dysfunction reported; no fever.
- Physical exam: Decreased right ankle reflex, positive straight leg raise test on the right.
- Social history: Patient works as a manual laborer, no smoking or alcohol use documented.
- Differential diagnosis:
  - Lumbar disc herniation (High) – classic radicular symptoms plus positive straight leg raise.
  - Spinal stenosis (Moderate) – less likely without neurogenic claudication or bilateral symptoms.
  - Cauda equina syndrome (Low) – no bladder/bowel symptoms, no saddle anesthesia.
  - Piriformis syndrome (Low) – no specific sciatic nerve irritation signs beyond radiculopathy.

Issue 2: None reported in transcript.

Issue 3: None reported in transcript.

Medications:
- Ibuprofen dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- None mentioned.

Past Medical History:
- None mentioned.

Social History:
- Manual labor occupation.
- No tobacco or alcohol use mentioned.

Preventative History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Decreased right ankle reflex.
- Positive straight leg raise test on right leg.
- No vitals recorded.

Plan:
- Advise analgesia with ibuprofen.
- Order lumbar spine MRI for further evaluation.
- Refer to neurology for assessment.
- Advise patient to monitor for bladder or bowel dysfunction and seek immediate care if symptoms develop.
- Follow-up after MRI results.
